behavior: Runs rapidly with advancing and retreating waves, picking prey from the surface and probing wet sand for small invertebrates; often forages and roosts in flocks.
field_marks: Small, plump shorebird with a rounded body
Straight, stout black bill about as long as the head
Round dark eye set in a plain, pale face
Pale gray upperparts and clean white underparts in nonbreeding plumage; juveniles show checkered upperparts
Long, pointed wings and a short tail; a bold white wing stripe shows in flight
habitat: Primarily wave-washed sandy beaches, tideflats, mudflats, rocky shores, and occasional inland lakeshores during migration and the nonbreeding season; breeds on exposed gravel, rocky ridges, and low-growing tundra near ponds or other wet areas.
